name: Geometric Topology

papers.title: The Transverse Finiteness Conjecture for pseudo-Anosov flows via universal circles
papers.abstract: We prove Mosher's Transverse Finiteness Conjecture, posed in 1996. This states that every taut, finite depth foliation $\mathcal F$ of an atoroidal 3-manifold is almost transverse to at most finitely many pseudo-Anosov flows, up to orbit equivalence. Our strategy is to organize the flows that are almost transverse to $\mathcal F$ using their associated universal circles. This technique also establishes the following rigidity result: if a finite depth foliation $\mathcal F$ is almost transverse to a pseudo-Anosov flow $\varphi$ without perfect fits, then $\varphi$ is the unique pseudo-Anosov flow that is almost transverse to $\mathcal F$, up to orbit equivalence. In fact, in this setting, $\mathcal F$ has only one minimal universal circle.

papers.title: Size-preserving Cromwell equivalence for unknotted grid diagrams
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that every grid diagram representing the unknot is equivalent, via Cromwell moves which preserve the grid number, to a grid diagram with no crossings, sharpening a monotonic-simplification result of Dynnikov. Moreover, we enumerate the equivalence classes of grid diagrams for the unknot, considered up to size-preserving Cromwell moves. As an application, we generate all grid diagrams for the unknot through grid number $8$ and identify the first examples of weakly Cromwell hard grid diagrams for the unknot.

papers.title: Norm groups of orders and the algebraic unknotting number
papers.abstract: We use number-theoretic tools to find an explicit and effective obstruction for a knot to have algebraic unknotting number equal to $1$. As an example, we show that the connected sum of $T(2,5)$ (the cinquefoil) and $-T(2,3)$ (the negative trefoil) has algebraic unknotting number $1$, even though $T(2,5)$ has algebraic unknotting number $2$.

papers.title: A Short Proof of the Goldman--Parker Conjecture
papers.abstract: Goldman and Parker conjectured that the three order-two complex side reflections of an ideal triangle with Cartan angular invariant $A$ define a discrete and faithful representation of $\mathbb Z/2 \ast \mathbb Z/2 \ast \mathbb Z/2$ in $PU(2,1)$ whenever $\tan^2 A\le 125/3$. Schwartz first proved the conjecture using rigorous computer-assisted estimates and later gave an analytic proof based on three loxodromic $\mathbb R$-spheres. We give a substantially shorter proof of this conjecture using a simpler geometric construction. For parameters just below the critical value, we use the Cygan bisector of the two fixed points of the triple product of the reflections. This wall and one of its cusp translates bound a strip from which we construct a trapping region. At the critical value $\tan^2 A=125/3$, the two fixed points merge, and the same construction applies to the limiting wall.

papers.title: Ergodicity of the mapping class group action on components with small nonzero Euler number
papers.abstract: We study the action of the mapping class group on the $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ character variety of a closed oriented surface of genus $g$. On the components considered here, the infimum of the translation lengths of essential simple closed curves is zero almost everywhere for every invariant positive Radon measure. For Goldman measure we show that almost every character sends some such curve to a non-hyperbolic element. By the criterion of Marche and Wolff, this proves Goldman's ergodicity conjecture for $g\ge 3$ and Euler numbers $e$ with $0<|e|\leq g-1$.

papers.title: Miyazawa invariants of satellite surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove formulas describing the behavior of Miyazawa's degree invariant of knotted spheres and real projective planes in the 4-sphere under satellite operations. As an application, we show that every deform-spun real projective plane admits infinitely many topologically but not smoothly isotopic copies. In particular, we produce an infinite exotic family of irreducible real projective planes containing Hughes-Kim-Miller-Nahm's counterexample to the Kinoshita conjecture.

papers.title: A fake quadric that is not a bidisk quotient
papers.abstract: Fake quadrics are minimal complex surfaces of general type with $b_1=0$ and $e=4$. The paper gives a construction of a fake quadric $S$ that is a $32$-fold branched cover of $\mathbf{CP}^1\times\mathbf{CP}^1$ along nine curves. This configuration is given by four horizontal lines, four vertical lines and the diagonal. We show that $S$ is not aspherical. As a corollary the universal cover of $S$ is not the bidisk $\mathbf{H}\times\mathbf{H}$.

papers.title: Fixed points for actions of automorphism groups of free products on ${\rm CAT(0)}$ spaces
papers.abstract: We study fixed-point properties of automorphism groups of free products acting on complete ${\rm CAT(0)}$ spaces. Under the assumption of certain fixed-point properties of the free factors, we obtain lower bounds on the smallest dimension in which automorphism groups can act on a complete ${\rm CAT(0)}$ space without a global fixed point.

papers.title: Colored Jones polynomial of figure eight knot and non-perturbative topological recursion
papers.abstract: The asymptotic expansion of the colored Jones polynomial of the figure eight knot is proved to be connected with non-perturbative topological recursion on the underlying elliptic spectral curve, following the proposal of Borot and Eynard.

papers.title: Counting Classical Fullerenes I: Exact Enumeration and Generic Achiral Symmetry
papers.abstract: We give an exact arithmetic formula for the number of classical fullerenes on $2m$ vertices. The oriented count is known; the new contribution counts achiral fullerenes, those admitting an orientation-reversing symmetry. We transport these symmetries to a lattice, classify eleven types, and express their contribution as seven weighted orbit counts. The complete formula is printed here, together with an exact algorithm producing all counts through index $M$ in quasilinear bit time with fast integer multiplication. We also prove that the proportion of achiral fullerenes with a unique orientation-reversing symmetry tends to one as the size increases. That symmetry is either a reflection or a fixed-point-free involution, with cumulative proportions $527/529$ and $2/529$. Among all fullerenes on $2m$ vertices, the achiral proportion has order $m^{-5}$; the same order holds cumulatively. The exceptional achiral classes with nontrivial orientation-preserving symmetry number $O(m^2)$.

papers.title: A non-Morse relatively Anosov group
papers.abstract: We construct a relatively Anosov group that is not relatively Morse.
